rows.label: Passive Recon
rows.value: Information gathering with ZERO contact with target systems. No packets sent. No logs created on the target. Read-only access to public sources. Legal without a contract. The Ghost mode.

rows.label: Active Recon
rows.value: Information gathering by directly interacting with the target's infrastructure. Packets sent, logs created, target may detect the activity. Requires explicit written authorisation. The Visitor mode.

rows.label: OSINT
rows.value: Open Source Intelligence. All intelligence gathered from publicly available sources. Always passive by definition. The foundation of Phase 1 in every professional engagement.

rows.label: WHOIS / who.is
rows.value: Domain registration records: owner, registrar, registration date, name servers. First stop for any domain-based target.

rows.label: crt.sh
rows.value: Certificate Transparency log search. Reveals every subdomain that has ever received an SSL certificate — including internal staging and development environments.

rows.label: LinkedIn
rows.value: Employee names, job titles, team structure, technology skills listed. One of the richest human-layer intelligence sources available.

rows.label: Job Postings
rows.value: Reveals the exact technology stack in use: security tools, cloud platforms, frameworks, internal systems. Companies list these publicly to attract candidates.

rows.label: Shodan.io
rows.value: Search engine for internet-connected devices. Reading cached Shodan data is passive. Triggering a new Shodan scan of a specific target is active.

rows.label: HaveIBeenPwned
rows.value: Checks if a company's email domain has appeared in known breach databases. Confirms exposure and reveals real employee email addresses.

rows.label: GitHub Search
rows.value: Search public repositories for the company name, domain, or email format. Often reveals accidentally committed credentials, API keys, and internal naming conventions.

rows.label: archive.org
rows.value: Historical website snapshots. Old versions of a website sometimes contain more information than the current version: staff directories, internal links, technology headers.

rows.label: Google Dorking
rows.value: Advanced search operators: site:target.com, filetype:pdf, intitle:"index of", inurl:admin. Finds publicly indexed sensitive pages and files.

rows.label: Digital Footprint
rows.value: The total trail of data an organisation has left across the internet — intentionally and incidentally. Assembled through OSINT. The larger the footprint, the larger the attack surface.

rows.label: Attack Surface
rows.value: Every potential entry point for an attacker: public web properties, APIs, remote access, cloud services, vendors, employees, legacy systems. Extends beyond the organisation's own perimeter.

rows.label: Supply Chain Vector
rows.value: Using a vendor or third party with target access as an entry point into the primary target — often easier due to weaker security controls. The Target/Fazio breach is the canonical example.

rows.label: Step 1
rows.value: Passive OSINT — exhaust all public sources before any active technique. Build the target dossier: technology stack, employees, subdomains, breach history, vendor relationships.

rows.label: Step 2
rows.value: Analyse and organise — structure the OSINT findings into categories. Identify the most likely attack vectors before touching a single tool.

rows.label: Step 3
rows.value: Confirm authorisation — verify that every technique planned for the active phase is explicitly covered by the scope agreement.

rows.label: Step 4
rows.value: Active reconnaissance — with the passive picture complete and authorisation confirmed, begin structured active enumeration targeting the highest-priority attack vectors.
